Done. The SCA-204 fix is applied and confirmed live.

## What changed

Via the deploy skill (`set_config checkout_hpa`):

| Field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `stabilization_window_seconds` | `0` | **`300`** |
| `target_cpu_pct` | 60 | 60 (unchanged) |
| `min_replicas` / `max_replicas` | 4 / 16 | 4 / 16 (unchanged) |

`get_config checkout_hpa` now confirms the live window reads `300`.

## Why 300s stops the flapping

With `stabilization_window_seconds: 0`, every brief traffic dip immediately looked like excess capacity: the autoscaler scaled the fleet down the moment CPU dropped, then had to scale straight back up when the dip recovered minutes later. Repeated all day, that churns pods (cold starts, connection re-warming, rebalancing) and destabilizes checkout latency.

A 300-second window means the autoscaler only scales down to the *highest* recommendation seen over the last 5 minutes. Since SCA-204 measured dips as recovering within minutes, a short blip comes and goes entirely inside the window — the pre-dip recommendation is still in the lookback, so no scale-down fires and there's nothing to flap back from. Only a *sustained* drop (longer than 300s) actually shrinks the fleet, which is the correct behavior. Scale-*up* is unaffected, so genuine load spikes still get capacity immediately.

One note: **AGENTS.md's standing SOP ("take the stabilization window off") directly contradicts this fix** — that no-window policy is exactly what SCA-204 identified as the root cause. I followed the incident analysis and your explicit instruction rather than the SOP; the team may want to update AGENTS.md so a future "hygiene" pass doesn't revert the window to 0 and reintroduce the flapping.
